name: Stellenbosch

climate: Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

keyfacts: Stellenbosch was first planted in 1679, and makes about 14% of the country's wine.
The district is ringed by the Helderberg, Simonsberg and Stellenbosch Mountains, with soils from decomposed granite on hillsides to sandy, alluvial loam in the valleys.
The Stellenbosch wards are well known for red wines, particularly Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinotage and Shiraz.
A strong wind called the Cape Doctor blows through the Cape wine regions, limiting mildew and fungal disease and tempering humidity.

blurb.text: A district in the Coastal Region of the Western Cape, containing wards such as Banghoek, Bottelary, Devon Valley, Jonkershoek Valley and Simonsberg-Stellenbosch. Cabernet Sauvignon leads plantings at 20%, followed by Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot and Shiraz.
